questions.question: What should you do if you must drive in high winds?

options.text: Relax your grip on the steering wheel.
Drive faster.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: A school bus's long sides can be pushed by wind. In windy conditions, grip the steering wheel firmly, watch for wind gusts, and slow down. If needed, contact your dispatcher for guidance.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Tell students when it is safe to board.
Count students and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.
Check mirrors for students running toward the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Students must always board a school bus in a single-file line.

questions.question: Loading a school bus:

options.text: Is not dangerous.
Does not need supervision.
Should be done quickly.
Can be dangerous.

questions.explanation: More students are killed loading or unloading school buses than riding in them. School bus drivers must follow safety procedures during loading and unloading.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and the bus must be evacuated, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby building
To the closest tree
Near a river
To a mountain

questions.explanation: If a tornado is approaching, take students to shelter in a nearby building. If no building is available, go to a ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood and stay far enough away so the bus cannot fall on them.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up students:

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students anywhere they are waiting.
Parents should decide where the bus stop will be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver should only pick up and drop off students at designated stops approved by the school district.

questions.question: A blind spot behind a school bus extends at least ____ feet.
questions.explanation: A school bus has blind spots below the mirrors, in front of the mirrors, and directly behind the bumper. Rear blind spots usually extend 50 to 150 feet behind the bus, but can extend up to 400 feet depending on the bus length.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, the driver should ensure all traffic has stopped before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling students to approach.
Turning on the flashing red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling students to approach.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, make sure all surrounding traffic has stopped before opening the door and signaling students to approach the bus.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Move down the stairs quickly.

questions.explanation: When exiting your bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the bus and maintain three points of contact at all times. Keep contact with the handrail. Incorrect exit may result in automatic test failure.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must show all of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if present, rises to normal operating range.
That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during a vehicle inspection, make sure it is working. The gauge should show normal pressure or the warning light should turn off. If the bus has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.explanation: When exiting your bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the bus and maintain three points of contact at all times. Keep contact with the handrail. Incorrect exit may result in automatic test failure.

questions.question: How far behind the bus should a bus operator be able to see with properly adjusted outside mirrors?

options.text: One bus length
Two bus lengths
Three bus lengths
Four bus lengths

questions.explanation: The side mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet (about four bus lengths) behind the bus.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you check in the fifth wheel gap?

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the coupling between a tractor and trailer, look into the fifth wheel gap and check that the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: How should you complete a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull forward directly into the parking space.
Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parallel parking maneuver on the driver's side, drive past the parking space first, then back into it. Position the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must stay within the space boundaries.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what might happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your on-road driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct procedures at a simulated location.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are present.
Check traffic only in the direction of the turn.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during your on-road driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which of the following does NOT need to be identified?

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water pump belt.
The alternator belt.
The water compressor belt.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for damage and tightness. If any of these items are not belt-driven, tell the examiner which ones and confirm they work properly and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: What should you do when inspecting engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: The belts should be checked for snugness, each with up to three inches of play.
The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
The air compressor belt should be removed.
Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: When checking engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test, check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for damage and tightness (up to three-quarters inch of play at the center). If any items are not belt-driven, identify them and confirm they work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Check for traffic.
Do not use signals.
Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, when entering an expressway, check traffic first, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: What counts as points against you during the basic control skills test?

options.text: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
Pulling up one time.
Exiting the vehicle one time to check your positioning.
Setting the parking brake.

questions.explanation: The examiner will count every time your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each touch or crossing counts as an error and is subtracted from your skills test score.
